examples.en: My house is southeast of the school.
A lot of sunlight comes in through the southeast window.
The typhoon is moving up from the southeast.
Point to the southeast on the map.

examples.ko: 동남쪽으로 십 분쯤 걸으면 역이 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk southeast for about ten minutes, you'll reach the station.
The sky cleared up first in the southeast.

explain: 동쪽과 남쪽 사이의 방향이에요. '남동쪽'이라고도 말해요. 반대 방향은 '서북쪽'이에요.

phrases.en: Our school is southeast of City Hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동남쪽'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the same meaning as 동남쪽.

phrases.example: 이 길로 동남쪽으로 가면 공원이 나와요.
phrases.en: If you go southeast on this road, you'll reach the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 안내할 때 방향을 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for giving directions.

phrases.en: A cold wind is blowing from the northwest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동남쪽'의 반대 방향을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite direction of 동남쪽.

explain_en: It is the direction between east and south. People also say '남동쪽'. The opposite direction is '서북쪽'.

en: to be easy; to be simple

examples.ko: 이 정도 비는 우산 없이도 문제없어요.
examples.en: Rain this light is no problem even without an umbrella.

examples.ko: 제가 도와 드릴 테니까 문제없을 거예요.
examples.en: I'll help you, so it won't be a problem.
If the schedule works, I'll start next week.

examples.ko: 검사 결과는 모두 문제없는 것으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: The test results all came out fine.
As long as you keep to the appointment time, it's fine.
Is it okay to play games on this computer?

explain: '문제가 없다'와 같은 뜻인데, 붙여서 한 단어로 써요. '괜찮아요'보다 기능이나 조건, 상태에 이상이 없다고 확인해 주는 느낌이에요. 상대가 걱정할 때 '네, 문제없어요'라고 짧게 대답하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Yes, this much is no problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 걱정할 때 짧게 대답하는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short polite reply when someone is worried.

phrases.en: Yesterday's presentation went without a problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일에 문제가 없었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say there was no problem in a past event.

phrases.en: If there is no problem, I'll start now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건을 말할 때 '-(으)면'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -(으)면 to make a condition.

explain_en: It means the same as '문제가 없다' but is written as one word. Compared with '괜찮아요', it feels more like confirming that a function, condition or state has no issue. You can also answer a worried person briefly with '네, 문제없어요'.

examples.en: Please try out the new program first.
We tested this machine at the factory yesterday.
The teacher sometimes tests the students' ability.
It's not good to test your friends.

examples.ko: 새 신발이 편한지 시험하려고 하루 종일 신었어요.
examples.en: I wore the new shoes all day to see if they were comfortable.

examples.ko: 처음 만든 로봇을 시험할 날이 왔어요.
examples.en: The day to test the first robot I built has come.

explain: 명사 '시험'은 학교 시험이라서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 시험을 치르는 건 '시험을 보다'이고, 새것이 잘 되는지 해 보는 건 '시험하다'예요. 보통 '시험해 보다'로 써요. 사람의 마음이나 실력을 일부러 떠볼 때도 '시험하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 새 기계를 먼저 시험해 보고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to test the new machine first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시험하다'는 보통 '-아/어 보다'와 함께 쓰고, 여기에 '-고 싶다'를 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '시험하다' usually goes with '-아/어 보다', and here '-고 싶다' is added.
phrases.en_equiv: I want to try testing it

phrases.en: I test the microphone in advance before the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본격적으로 쓰기 전에 잘 되는지 해 볼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for checking that something works before real use.

phrases.example: 친구가 제 마음을 시험하는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: It seems my friend is testing my feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 마음을 일부러 떠볼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone deliberately probes another person's feelings.

explain_en: The noun '시험' usually means a school exam, which causes confusion. Taking an exam is '시험을 보다', while '시험하다' is trying something to see if it works, usually as '시험해 보다'. It can also mean deliberately testing a person's heart or ability.

dis.h: try out ability or quality; general

p.n: Same meaning; the replacement is a loanword and sounds more technical.

en: to settle in; to take root; to become established

examples.ko: 새 제도가 현장에 잘 정착되고 있어요.
examples.en: The new system is taking root well on site.
The culture of sorting recycling has taken hold in every apartment complex.

examples.ko: 이 제도가 정착된 지 벌써 오 년이에요.
examples.en: It has already been five years since this system took root.
A new culture only takes root as time passes.
It takes about a month for a habit to settle in.

examples.ko: 새 규칙이 학교에 정착되는 데 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took time for the new rule to take root at the school.

explain: 사람이 한 곳에 자리 잡으면 '정착하다', 제도, 문화, 습관이 자리 잡으면 '정착되다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '자리 잡다'도 자주 말해요. 주어가 사람이냐 제도냐에 따라 골라 쓰세요.

phrases.en: I settled down in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person is the subject.

phrases.en: The new habit has taken hold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday expression.

phrases.en: This culture has not yet become established.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 자리 잡지 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it has not yet taken hold.

explain_en: When a person settles in a place, use '정착하다'; when a system, culture or habit takes root, use '정착되다'. In casual talk people also say '자리 잡다'. Choose by whether the subject is a person or a system.

en: Chuseok day; the day of Chuseok

examples.ko: 추석날에는 온 가족이 모여서 송편을 빚어요.
examples.en: On Chuseok day, the whole family gathers to make songpyeon.

examples.ko: 추석날 아침에 일찍 일어나서 차례를 지내요.
examples.en: On the morning of Chuseok, we get up early and hold the ancestral rite.
It's a shame that Chuseok day overlaps with the weekend.

examples.ko: 추석날 길이 막힐까 봐 하루 전에 출발했어요.
examples.en: I left a day early, worried the roads would be jammed on Chuseok day.
This year on Chuseok day the moon was very bright.
There are people who work even on Chuseok day.

explain: '추석'은 명절 전체를 가리킬 때도 있고, '추석날'은 음력 8월 15일 그날을 콕 집어 말해요. 연휴 전체는 '추석 연휴'라고 해요. '설날'과 같이 날짜를 말하는 '-날' 표현이에요.

phrases.en: On the morning of Chuseok, I wore hanbok.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명절 당일의 아침을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the morning of the holiday itself.

phrases.en: I went to my hometown during the Chuseok holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그날 하루가 아니라 쉬는 기간 전체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the whole holiday period, not just the day.

phrases.en: The full moon on Chuseok was very bright.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추석은 음력 8월 15일이라 보름달과 함께 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Chuseok falls on a full-moon day, so they often go together.

explain_en: '추석' can refer to the whole holiday, while '추석날' pinpoints the day itself, the 15th of the 8th lunar month. The whole break is called '추석 연휴'. Like '설날', it's a '-날' word naming a particular day.

examples.en: The river rose, so traffic on the bridge was closed off.

examples.ko: 마라톤 때문에 시청 앞 도로가 통제돼요.
examples.en: The road in front of City Hall is closed because of the marathon.

examples.ko: 사고가 나서 고속도로 일부가 통제되고 있어요.
examples.en: Part of the highway is closed due to an accident.

examples.ko: 공연장 입구는 한 시간 전부터 통제되었어요.
examples.en: The entrance to the venue has been restricted since an hour ago.

examples.ko: 그곳은 허가 없이는 출입이 통제되는 곳이에요.
examples.en: That is a place where entry is restricted without permission.

examples.ko: 감정이 통제되지 않아서 크게 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: I couldn't control my emotions and got very angry.

explain: 길, 출입, 차량처럼 누군가 정해서 막거나 제한할 때 써요. 저절로 막힌 '막히다'와 달리 사람의 결정이 있어요. 하는 쪽은 '통제하다'이고, 감정이나 행동에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The police close off the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막는 쪽이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the party blocking is the subject.

phrases.en: Entry is restricted because of construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어가고 나가는 것을 막을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when entering and leaving are blocked.

phrases.en: It's hard to control my anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이나 행동에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used for emotions and behavior.

explain_en: It is used when someone decides to block or restrict things like roads, entry and vehicles. Unlike '막히다', which just means blocked, there is a person's decision behind it. The acting side uses '통제하다', and it can also apply to emotions and behavior.

dis.h: be restricted or closed off by authority

p.n: 제어되다 is for machines and systems, not a road closed to people.

examples.en: In the morning, the sun came out from behind the clouds.

examples.ko: 아이가 해님을 그리고 웃는 얼굴을 넣었어요.
examples.en: The child drew the sun and gave it a smiling face.
Thanks to the sun, the laundry dried quickly.

examples.ko: 해님, 달님 이야기를 아이에게 읽어 줬어요.
examples.en: I read the child the story of the sun and the moon.
It is a baby who smiles as brightly as the sun.
In the fairy tale, the sun and the wind made a bet.

explain: '해'에 '님'을 붙여 해를 사람처럼 다정하게 부르는 말이에요. 동화, 동요, 아이에게 하는 말에서 잘 나오고, 어른이 날씨를 말할 때는 보통 그냥 '해'라고 해요. '달님'과 짝이에요.

phrases.en: The sun rose and the sky got bright.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이 날씨를 말할 때 쓰는 보통 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The plain word adults use when talking about weather.

phrases.en: I get up when the sun rises in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동요나 동화처럼 다정한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a warm feel, like in songs and children's stories.

phrases.en: My younger sibling drew the sun in yellow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이의 그림 이야기에서 잘 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears when talking about children's drawings.

explain_en: Adding '님' to '해' addresses the sun warmly, as if it were a person. It shows up in fairy tales, children's songs and talk with kids, while adults usually just say '해' when discussing the weather. Its partner word is '달님'.
